name: Delbáeth
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Delbáeth was an obscure Irish goddess. Her name means "fire-shape." The Book of Invasions names her as the mother of Donand. Many writers believe Donand is the same as Danu, the goddess of earth. A second figure shared the name Delbáeth. This one was a druid of the hill of Uisneach. He built a great fire. Five points of light streamed outward from that fire.
objective: This entry records Delbáeth, an obscure Irish fire goddess and mother of Donand.
